aggregate_metrics.ADPR_denominator: All dependency_points unless a paper section explicitly reports primary_async_dependency_ids only.
aggregate_metrics.minimum_success_condition_for_task_level: Both primary_async_dependency_ids pass in the final integrated workspace.

annotation_notes: The query_to_table dependency is the primary async signal because the state-stack worker can implement Table search and caching against stale Query and LRUCache assumptions.
The operations_to_table dependency captures transform/update behavior that can be locally plausible but fail once query and table artifacts are integrated.
The state-stack shared-mapping dependency records integration-level storage, table, TinyDB, and middleware state consistency.
These labels identify public test-observable contracts and implicated files, not solution code.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Table search and TinyDB search must consume Query equality/hash behavior, frozen query values, and LRUCache semantics consistently for query caching and repeated lookup.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when query/cache producer probes and table/TinyDB query-cache consumer probes pass in the integrated workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The state-stack worker may implement table search or query caching around stale Query hashing, equality, or LRUCache semantics, yielding late integrated failures without textual conflicts.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Table and TinyDB update paths must consume operation transform functions such as set, delete, increment, and decrement with the same mutation and return-value semantics.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when operation-function probes and TinyDB update consumer probes pass after integration.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The state-stack worker may assume transforms return a new document or mutate in place differently from the final operations artifact, producing integrated update failures after a clean merge.

dependency_points.contract_summary: Storage, Table, TinyDB, and CachingMiddleware must agree on the complete database mapping, table names, document IDs, read/write lifecycle, and cache flush behavior.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when storage/middleware probes and integrated TinyDB/table state probes pass in the final workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The state-stack artifact may pass narrower storage or table tests while leaving the complete-database mapping or cache flush contract inconsistent across integrated TinyDB APIs.

evaluation_checkpoint_policy.minimum_policy: Run probe tests after each agent final artifact and after final integration.
evaluation_checkpoint_policy.recommended_policy: Run probe tests after every committed patch, every explicit artifact transfer, and final integration.

ADPR.definition: Fraction of registered dependency_points whose required integrated_probe_tests pass in the final integrated workspace.
ADPR.name: Async Dependency Pass Rate

CAIL.definition: downstream_resolution_step minus upstream_resolution_step when both probe groups have been evaluated.
CAIL.name: Cross-Agent Integration Lag

DRS.definition: First recorded checkpoint at which all required integrated_probe_tests for a dependency point pass.
DRS.name: Dependency Resolution Step

SAD.definition: Interval during which a downstream worker acts on a contract assumption inconsistent with the latest upstream artifact visible in the integrated history.
SAD.name: Stale Assumption Duration

purpose: Dependency-level labels for measuring whether asynchronous multi-agent coding resolves TinyDB's query, table, storage, database, and middleware contracts promptly.
